title: UNIX V7: finding your way
text: In the tested V7 guest, pwd prints the working directory, ls lists directory entries, and cat displays a text file. The shell and commands run in the guest; a browser terminal is only their input/output surface. Start with a listing before editing a disposable file. These examples were exercised in the project laboratory, not inferred from the currently selected terminal label.
question: Explain pwd, ls and the UNIX root directory to a beginner.

title: RT-11: a different command environment
text: The project's owner-operated RT-11SJ V05.03 baseline accepted DIR and SHOW CONFIG. That is recorded evidence for that guest, not a claim that every RT-11 version has identical commands or drivers. Do not substitute UNIX command syntax by assumption. Confirm the running guest and consult its matching manual before writing files or changing devices.
question: Explain how an RT-11 session differs from a UNIX shell.

title: RSX-11M: command context matters
text: DEC's RSX-11M Beginner's Guide (June 1977), section 3.2.1, describes the Peripheral Interchange Program (PIP) and its /LI directory-listing switch. Its command language and file naming differ from UNIX. Identify the installed RSX version and command interpreter before adapting an example; this project has not qualified an RSX browser tutor session.
question: Explain PIP and why RSX examples should not be pasted into a UNIX shell.

title: 2.11BSD: terminals and vi
text: The laboratory's 2.11BSD media contains /usr/ucb/vi and /usr/ucb/more. /usr must be mounted before checking those paths. The guest TERM setting and the browser's terminal personality must agree. The project's vi workflow uses a disposable file, insert mode, Escape, :w, Ctrl-L redraw, :wq, and readback; the browser never rewrites the guest program.
question: Explain vi command mode, insert mode and TERM using a disposable file.

title: Octal and PDP-11 instruction words
text: Octal uses digits 0 through 7. One octal digit represents three binary bits: octal 17 equals decimal 15. PDP-11 instruction words are 16 bits, often written in octal; an address radix must be stated explicitly. MOV copies a source operand to a destination using specified addressing modes. The device lab's MOVB polling programs exercise device registers; they are not OS printer drivers.
question: Work through octal 17 plus 1, then explain MOV versus MOVB at a beginner level.

title: Printer, paper tape and observation
text: Original SIMH owns LP11 and PC11 behavior. A device existing in SIMH does not prove a guest OS has its driver. Host-visible output may lag CPU writes because the simulator buffers files. Observation is read-only and requires explicit producer identity; an inactive browser does not imply a stopped CPU. PC11 reader input and punch output are separate media, and byte counts alone do not prove end-of-tape.
question: Explain printer spooling and the difference between a paper-tape reader and punch.
